# Implementation Plan: WhatsApp Session Routing, A/B Variant Testing & Production Automation Engine This plan addresses the end-to-end architecture, user flow, and configuration gaps across **Workflow Creation**, **WhatsApp Number/Session Association**, **Wasender API & Webhook Authentication**, **Variant Testing & Activation**, and **Media Upload/Preview**. --- ## 1. Executive Summary & Problem Analysis Based on our architectural deep-dive into the codebase (`@wastat/server`, `@wastat/web`, `@wastat/shared`), the following key findings and gaps were identified: 1. **Missing Session/Number Selection in Workflows**: - `packages/shared/src/types.ts` defines `sessionId?: number` on `WorkflowDefinition`, but the database table `workflows` (`schema.sql` and Supabase migrations) lacks the `session_id` column. - Workflows cannot be scoped to a specific WhatsApp number (e.g. Sales Desk vs Support Number) in the UI. - When an incoming message arrives at `/webhooks/wasender/:providerSessionId`, `engine.ts` tests triggers against *all* active workflows instead of filtering for `workflow.session_id IS NULL OR workflow.session_id = sessionId`. 2. **Wasender API & Webhook Fragility**: - Inbound webhook processing (`app.ts`) rejected requests with HTTP 401 if `session.webhook_secret` was empty/null in the DB. - Phone number extraction parsed `remoteJid.split('@')[0]`, which fails when WhatsApp sends Linked IDs (`@lid`) instead of true MSISDNs. Wasender explicitly provides `cleanedSenderPn` and `cleanedParticipantPn` in the payload. - Wasender PAT vs Session Key: Account-level operations (listing sessions, QR codes) use `WASENDER_PAT`, while message sending and session-specific webhooks use the session's individual API key (`api_key_encrypted`). The app needs to support both PAT auto-sync and manual session entry (for users who configure session keys directly). 3. **A/B Variant Testing & Activation Journey**: - An Experiment is a collection of workflow variants (`workflows.experiment_id = experiment.id`). - Sticky routing in `engine.ts` assigns incoming contacts to variants and tracks funnel conversions. - In `Experiments.tsx`, users could view funnel statistics and z-test calculations, but could not directly toggle a variant workflow's active/live state or navigate seamlessly between the experiment dashboard and the canvas editor. 4. **Media Upload & Preview Integration**: - Cloudflare R2 / Local fallback backend (`media.ts`) and upload endpoints exist. - In `WorkflowEditor.tsx`, `send_media` config form includes file upload and image preview, but canvas nodes only display `Asset #id` text rather than a thumbnail preview. --- ## 2. User Review Required > [!IMPORTANT] > **Workflow Scope Model**: > We will implement **Global vs Session-Specific Workflows**: > - `session_id = NULL`: Workflow triggers on messages from **all connected numbers** (Default). > - `session_id = `: Workflow triggers **only** on messages received by that specific WhatsApp number/session. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Webhook Security Graceful Mode**: > If a session in Wasender has a `webhook_secret` configured, Wasender sends `X-Webhook-Signature` which is strictly verified. If no secret is configured on the session, requests are accepted with session verification via `:providerSessionId` route param, preventing false 401 rejections in production. --- ## 3. Architecture & User Flow Design ```mermaid flowchart TD subgraph Inbound Journey A[Customer sends WhatsApp msg] --> B[Wasender Gateway] B -->|POST webhook /webhooks/wasender/:providerSessionId| C[WaStat Server] C --> D{Verify Session & Secret} D -->|Valid| E[Extract cleanedSenderPn / ID] E --> F[Dedup by provider_message_id] F --> G[engine.handleIncomingMessage] end subgraph Trigger & Experiment Matching G --> H{In Waiting Input?} H -->|Yes| I[Advance Menu / Collect Input Node] H -->|No| J[Find Matching Trigger] J --> K[Filter Workflows:
w.active = 1 AND

Proposed Changes ### Component 1: Database Schema & Shared Types #### [MODIFY] [`packages/shared/src/types.ts`](file:///home/stevenjossu/wastat/packages/shared/src/types.ts) - Update `WorkflowDefinition` to include `sessionId?: number | null;` and `sessionName?: string;`. - Add `session_id INTEGER REFERENCES sessions(id) ON DELETE SET NULL` to `workflows` table. - Add index `CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_workflows_session ON workflows (session_id, active);`. #### [NEW] [`supabase/migrations/20260824000001_add_workflow_session_id.sql`](file:///home/stevenjossu/wastat/supabase/migrations/20260824000001_add_workflow_session_id.sql) - Add `ALTER TABLE workflows ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS session_id BIGINT REFERENCES sessions(id) ON DELETE SET NULL;`. --- ### Component 2: Server Engine, Webhook, and Wasender Transport #### [MODIFY] [`packages/server/src/app.ts`](file:///home/stevenjossu/wastat/packages/server/src/app.ts) - In webhook handler `/webhooks/wasender/:providerSessionId`: - Verify signature when `session.webhook_secret` is present: `if (session.webhook_secret && signature !== session.webhook_secret) return reply.code(401)...`. - Extract phone reliably: ```ts const key = body.data?.messages?.key; const phone = key.cleanedSenderPn || key.cleanedParticipantPn || key.remoteJid.replace(/@.*$/, ""); ``` - Pass `session.id` to `engine.handleIncomingMessage(session.id, contact.id, msg.id)`. #### [MODIFY] [`packages/server/src/engine.ts`](file:///home/stevenjossu/wastat/packages/server/src/engine.ts) - In `parseGraph`: accept `sessionId?: number | null`. - In `POST /api/workflows` and `PUT /api/workflows/:id`: insert/update `session_id`. - In `GET /api/workflows` and `GET /api/workflows/:id`: return `sessionId` and join `sessions.name AS sessionName`. - In `/api/sessions`: allow creating manual sessions with API key/secret and list associated workflow counts. --- ### Component 3: Web UI & Workflow Editor #### [MODIFY] [`packages/web/src/WorkflowList.tsx`](file:///home/stevenjossu/wastat/packages/web/src/WorkflowList.tsx) - Add WhatsApp Session dropdown to `CreateWorkflowForm` ("All Numbers (Global)" or specific connected session). - Display a session badge (e.g. `📱 Sales Desk (+123456789)`) on each workflow list row. #### [MODIFY] [`packages/web/src/WorkflowEditor.tsx`](file:///home/stevenjossu/wastat/packages/web/src/WorkflowEditor.tsx) - Add Session Selector in the top workflow editor toolbar next to the Live/Draft toggle. - Enhance custom `send_media` node on the React Flow canvas to render a rich image/video thumbnail preview when a media asset is selected. - In `FlowSimulatorModal`: allow testing the flow against specific session contexts and mock contact numbers. #### [MODIFY] [`packages/web/src/Sessions.tsx`](file:///home/stevenjossu/wastat/packages/web/src/Sessions.tsx) - Display assigned workflows count and direct links for each session. - Add "Manual Session Configuration" dialog (allowing input of `api_key` and `webhook_secret` directly for self-hosted or pre-created Wasender sessions). - Provide copy-to-clipboard for Webhook URLs with clear instructions. #### [MODIFY] [`packages/web/src/Experiments.tsx`](file:///home/stevenjossu/wastat/packages/web/src/Experiments.tsx) - Add quick Live/Draft toggle buttons for each variant workflow directly in the Variant Comparison Table. - # Implementation Plan: Inbound Webhook Engine, Humanized Replies, Execution Traceability & Session-Scoped Automations

This document presents the complete architectural blueprint and end-to-end user flows for WaStat V2, incorporating insights from `/home/stevenjossu/whatsapp-chatbot-saas` and addressing the execution visibility, auto-read, and typing presence requirements.

---

## 1. Executive Summary & Core Requirements

When an incoming WhatsApp message arrives via Wasender webhook, the platform must execute a humanized, predictable, and fully observable automation pipeline:

```
[Wasender Webhook] 
       │
       ▼
[1. Inbound Ingestion] ──► Dedup (provider_message_id) ──► Upsert Contact ──► Log Message
       │
       ▼
[2. Condition Evaluation] ──► Filter Active Workflows by Session/Number ──► Trigger Matching / Experiment Assignment
       │
       ├─► [No Match] ──► Log "No Trigger Matched" Event ──► Retain Inbound in Inbox
       │
       ▼ [Condition TRUE]
[3. Humanized Pre-Flight]
       ├─► Send Read Receipt (Blue Ticks) to WhatsApp (via markMessageAsRead API)
       └─► Send Typing Presence ("composing", 2-3s duration) (via sendPresenceUpdate API)
       │
       ▼
[4. Step-by-Step Node Execution] ──► Text / Media / Menu / Condition / Delay / Milestone
       │
       ▼
[5. Execution Tracking & Live Inspector] ──► Record Event Timeline in `events` ──► Viewable in UI
```

---

## 2. Key Architectural Components

### A. Inbound Webhook & Humanized Execution Engine (`@wastat/server`)
1. **Session & Number Scoping**:
   - Workflows can be bound to a specific WhatsApp number (`session_id`) or configured as Global (`session_id = NULL`).
   - Trigger evaluation only checks workflows active for that specific session or global workflows.
2. **Auto-Read (Blue Ticks) & Composing Presence**:
   - When a workflow trigger condition matches, before dispatching the reply:
     - The server immediately triggers `markMessageAsRead` (blue ticks).
     - The server issues a `sendPresenceUpdate(apiKey, toPhone, "composing")` with a humanized typing delay.
3. **Execution Event Timeline & Observability**:
   - Every execution records detailed step transitions in `events`:
     - `trigger.matched` (keyword, threshold, match algorithm)
     - `read_receipt.sent`
     - `presence.sent` (composing / recording)
     - `node.entered` (node_key, type, input config)
     - `node.completed` (output data, interpolated variables)
     - `condition.evaluated` (predicate, result: true/false, branch selected)
     - `execution.completed` / `execution.failed` (with error message)
   - REST API endpoints:
     - `GET /api/executions`: List recent executions with filters (`sessionId`, `workflowId`, `status`, `search`).
     - `GET /api/executions/:id`: Full execution drill-down (trigger message, sender contact, variable state, and step-by-step event timeline).

### B. User Experience & Frontend (`@wastat/web`)
1. **New "Executions / Automation Runs" Tab & Drawer**:
   - Complete live log of all incoming messages and their automation outcomes.
   - Status chips: `⚡ Matched & Completed`, `⏳ Waiting Input`, `🛑 Paused (Human Takeover)`, `⚠️ Failed`, `⚪ No Trigger Matched`.
   - Click any row to open the **Execution Trace Inspector Drawer** displaying:
     - Inbound message text & sender phone.
     - Target WhatsApp session name & number.
     - Workflow name & variant name (if in A/B experiment).
     - Variable inspector (`vars` snapshot).
     - Visual timeline of each node executed with timestamp and duration.
2. **Inbox Execution Badges**:
   - In `Inbox.tsx`, messages that triggered an automation display a clickable `⚡ Exec #ID` badge that immediately opens the execution trace.
3. **Workflow Creation & Editor Session Picker**:
   - Modal and Editor header allow picking target WhatsApp session (`All Numbers` vs `+123456789 (Sales Desk)`).
   - Live / Draft toggle for immediate activation.
   - Rich media thumbnail preview on custom `send_media` canvas nodes.
4. **Sessions Page**:
   - Shows connection status, QR code modal, active workflow count, and manual session key/secret editor.
5. **Experiments Page**:
   - Direct active/draft toggles for each variant workflow, statistical winner recommendation (Z-test), and Wilson confidence intervals.

---

## 3. End-to-End User Journeys

### Journey 1: Creating a Session-Specific Trigger Automation
1. Operator navigates to **Workflows** → clicks **New Workflow**.
2. Operator enters Name (e.g. `Price Enquiry (Sales Desk)`), selects WhatsApp Number (e.g. `Sales Desk (+123456789)`), and selects optional Experiment.
3. In the canvas editor, operator connects:
   - **Trigger Node**: Keyword `price`, exact match.
   - **Send Text Node**: `Hi {{contact.name}}! Our price is $49. Reply 1 for details.`
   - **End Node**.
4. Operator flips switch to **Live**.

### Journey 2: Customer Message Ingestion & Execution Inspection
1. Customer sends WhatsApp message: `"What is the price?"` to the Sales Desk number.
2. Wasender fires webhook to `POST /webhooks/wasender/:providerSessionId`.
3. WaStat server validates session, extracts `cleanedSenderPn`, logs message to `messages`.
4. Engine evaluates triggers for Sales Desk session -> Matches `Price Enquiry`.
5. Engine automatically marks message as **Read** (blue ticks) and sends **Typing Presence** for 2 seconds.
6. Engine sends outbound reply, updates execution status to `completed`, and records node events.
7. Operator visits **Executions** (or **Inbox**) in WaStat dashboard:
   - Sees the new execution row: `Price Enquiry • +123456789 • ⚡ Completed (2.1s)`.
   - Clicks to view the step-by-step trace showing trigger match, blue ticks, typing presence, and sent message payload.

---

## 4. Proposed File Changes

### Component 1: Shared Models & Types (`@wastat/shared`)

#### [MODIFY] [`packages/shared/src/types.ts`](file:///home/stevenjossu/wastat/packages/shared/src/types.ts)
- Add `sessionId?: number | null;` and `sessionName?: string;` to `WorkflowDefinition` and `WorkflowSummary`.
- Add execution trace models:
  ```ts
  export interface WorkflowExecutionSummary {
    id: number;
    workflowId: number;
    workflowName: string;
    sessionId: number;
    sessionName?: string;
    contactId: number;
    contactPhone: string;
    contactName?: string;
    triggerMessageId?: number;
    triggerText?: string;
    status: "running" | "waiting" | "waiting_input" | "paused_human" | "completed" | "failed" | "cancelled";
    currentNodeKey?: string | null;
    vars: Record<string, unknown>;
    startedAt: string;
    finishedAt?: string | null;
    durationMs?: number;
  }

  export interface ExecutionEventLog {
    id: number;
    executionId: number;
    eventType: string;
    nodeKey?: string;
    data: Record<string, unknown>;
    createdAt: string;
  }
  ```

---

### Component 2: Server Database & Engine (`@wastat/server`)

#### [MODIFY] [`packages/server/src/db/schema.sql`](file:///home/stevenjossu/wastat/packages/server/src/db/schema.sql)
- Add `session_id INTEGER REFERENCES sessions(id) ON DELETE SET NULL` to `workflows`.
- Add indexes for fast execution lookup:
  ```sql
  CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_workflows_session ON workflows (session_id, active);
  CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_events_execution_ordered ON events (execution_id, id ASC);
  ```

#### [NEW] [`supabase/migrations/20260824000001_add_workflow_session_id.sql`](file:///home/stevenjossu/supabase/migrations/20260824000001_add_workflow_session_id.sql)
- Supabase Postgres schema migration matching SQLite changes.

#### [MODIFY] [`packages/server/src/wasender.ts`](file:///home/stevenjossu/wastat/packages/server/src/wasender.ts)
- Export helper `sendPresenceUpdate` and `markMessageAsRead` to support pipeline execution.

#### [MODIFY] [`packages/server/src/app.ts`](file:///home/stevenjossu/wastat/packages/server/src/app.ts)
- In webhook handler `/webhooks/wasender/:providerSessionId`:
  - Extract phone reliably using `cleanedSenderPn || cleanedParticipantPn || remoteJid.replace(/@.*$/, "")`.
  - Validate webhook signature strictly when `session.webhook_secret` is configured, gracefully when not configured.
  - Ignore `fromMe: true` messages.
  - Call `engine.handleIncomingMessage(session.id, contact.id, msg.id)`.

#### [MODIFY] [`packages/server/src/engine.ts`](file:///home/stevenjossu/wastat/packages/server/src/engine.ts)
- Update `handleIncomingMessage`:
  - Query active workflows: `WHERE active = 1 AND (session_id IS NULL OR session_id = ?)`.
  - When matching workflow found:
    - Insert execution record with `trigger_message_id`.
    - Log `trigger.matched` event.
    - **Auto-Read**: Trigger `markMessageAsRead` on Wasender transport & log event.
    - **Composing Presence**: Trigger `sendPresenceUpdate("composing")` with delay.
  - Log every node step, branch decision, variable change, and completion into `events`.

#### [MODIFY] [`packages/server/src/api.ts`](file:///home/stevenjossu/wastat/packages/server/src/api.ts)
- Add CRUD support for `sessionId` in `POST /api/workflows` and `PUT /api/workflows/:id`.
- Add `GET /api/executions`: Paginated list with filters (`sessionId`, `workflowId`, `status`, `search`).
- Add `GET /api/executions/:id`: Full details, contact info, trigger message, and chronological event trace.
- Add `GET /api/executions/summary`: KPIs (total runs, success rate, waiting count).

---

### Component 3: Web UI (`@wastat/web`)

#### [NEW] [`packages/web/src/Executions.tsx`](file:///home/stevenjossu/wastat/packages/web/src/Executions.tsx)
- Dedicated Executions Activity Log page:
  - KPI banner: Total Executions, Completed, In-Flight / Waiting Input, Failed.
  - Search & filter bar: Filter by WhatsApp Number/Session, Workflow, Status, Date.
  - Live data table: Timestamp, Number/Session, Inbound Message, Triggered Workflow & Variant, Status, Duration.
  - **Slide-over Execution Trace Drawer**:
    - Timeline of all node steps with badges and timestamps.
    - Full payload & variable state inspector.
    - Direct link to open the workflow in the Canvas Editor.

#### [MODIFY] [`packages/web/src/WorkflowList.tsx`](file:///home/stevenjossu/wastat/packages/web/src/WorkflowList.tsx)

#### [MODIFY] [`packages/web/src/WorkflowEditor.tsx`](file:///home/stevenjossu/wastat/packages/web/src/WorkflowEditor.tsx)

#### [MODIFY] [`packages/web/src/Inbox.tsx`](file:///home/stevenjossu/wastat/packages/web/src/Inbox.tsx)

- Clicking the chip opens the Execution Trace modal directly from the Inbox.

#### [MODIFY] [`packages/web/src/Experiments.tsx`](file:///home/stevenjossu/wastat/packages/web/src/Experiments.tsx)

#### [MODIFY] [`packages/web/src/App.tsx`](file:///home/stevenjossu/wastat/packages/web/src/App.tsx)

---

### Automated Test Suite
- `npm run typecheck`: 0 errors across all 4 packages.
- `npm test`: 100% pass across shared, server, web, mcp-server.
  - Unit tests for session-scoped workflow filtering (`engine.test.ts`).
  - Unit tests for auto-read and presence triggering (`engine.test.ts`).
  - Unit tests for execution log retrieval endpoints (`api.test.ts`).
  - Unit tests for webhook `cleanedSenderPn` extraction and signature verification (`webhook.test.ts`).
- `npm run test:e2e`: full inbound message → session match → auto-read → typing presence → outbound reply → execution event log verification.

# Implementation Plan: Humanized WhatsApp Automation Pipeline, Payload Parameters & Workflow Lifecycle

This plan incorporates the required human-like behavioral pipeline, payload variable interpolation, workflow cloning/editing, and execution observability.

---

## 1. Human-Like Behavior & Timing Lifecycle

To avoid robotic detection and ban risks, the inbound-to-outbound execution follows a strict multi-stage timing sequence:

```
[Inbound WhatsApp Message Received]
                 │
                 ▼
  [Condition / Trigger Evaluation]
                 │
      ┌──────────┴──────────┐
      ▼                     ▼
[Condition FALSE]     [Condition TRUE]
      │                     │
      ▼                     ▼
• DO NOT mark as read  [Stage 1: Read Delay]
• DO NOT send typing   Wait 2–6s (simulates noticing notification & opening chat)
• DO NOT send reply         │
• Keep message unread       ▼
• Retain in Inbox      [Stage 2: Blue Ticks (mark_read)]
                       Dispatches markMessageAsRead
                            │
                            ▼
                       [Stage 3: Reaction Delay]
                       Wait 1–3s (simulates human reading & thinking)
                            │
                            ▼
                       [Stage 4: Typing Presence ("composing")]
                       Dispatches sendPresenceUpdate("composing") for 2–5s
                            │
                            ▼
                       [Stage 5: Message Dispatch (send_message)]
                       Dispatches the text / media / menu reply
                            │
                            ▼
                       [Stage 6: Subsequent Nodes]
                       Progress through workflow with configured delays
```

### Critical Humanization Guardrails:
1. **Unread Retention**: If no trigger condition matches, the conversation remains **unread** (no blue ticks sent) so human agents can see the unread message in their inbox.
2. **Read-Before-Send Rule**: No automated message is ever sent without first turning blue ticks on.
3. **No Simultaneous Read + Send**: The system will never fire read receipts and message sending at the same timestamp.
4. **Mandatory Composing Presence**: Every automated message is preceded by typing presence (`composing`).

---

## 2. Inbound Payload & Contact Variable Interpolation

All webhook metadata, contact profile information, and session data are normalized and exposed to template strings and Spintax in all message nodes:

| Template Variable | Description | Example Value |
|---|---|---|
| `{{contact.phone}}` or `{{contact.number}}` | Contact's international MSISDN | `+15551234567` |
| `{{contact.name}}` or `{{contact.pushName}}` | WhatsApp profile name / push name | `Marcus Aurelius` |
| `{{contact.id}}` | Database contact ID | `101` |
| `{{session.name}}` | WhatsApp device / number label | `Sales Desk #1` |
| `{{session.id}}` | WhatsApp session ID | `2` |
| `{{message.text}}` | The incoming trigger message body | `Hi, I need pricing` |
| `{{message.id}}` | WhatsApp provider message ID | `3EB0X123456789` |
| `{{contact.<attribute_name>}}` | Custom CRM contact attributes | `{{contact.budget}}` |
| `{{vars.<key>}}` | Workflow collected input variables | `{{vars.villa_preference}}` |

---

## 3. Workflow Management & Duplication

1. **Duplicate Workflow (1-Click Clone)**:
   - Available on the **Workflow List** page (action button) and in the **Workflow Editor** header.
   - Creates a full deep copy of the workflow graph (all nodes, configs, and edges).
   - Names the clone `${Original Name} (Copy)`.
   - Defaults the clone to `active: 0` (Draft) so it can be edited safely before going live.
2. **Edit Workflow**:
   - Full drag-and-drop React Flow canvas editor with session assignment, Live/Draft toggle, undo/redo, and interactive simulation.

---

## 4. Execution Traceability & Live Inspector

1. **`#/executions` Dashboard**:
   - Live log of every inbound WhatsApp message across all numbers.
   - Filter by Session, Workflow, Status (`Completed`, `Waiting Input`, `Failed`, `No Trigger Matched`), and Date.
   - Duration badge showing total elapsed time from message arrival to response delivery.
2. **Execution Trace Drawer**:
   - Step-by-step visual audit trail:
     - `15:02:01` 📥 Message Received: `"What is the price?"`
     - `15:02:03` 🔍 Trigger Matched: `Price Quote (Exact match, score 1.0)`

• session_id match OR global
• Direct vs Group message match] M --> N{Trigger Match Found?} N -->|No| O[Keep Conversation Unread
Log 'no_trigger_matched' event] N -->|Yes| P[Evaluate Experiment / Sticky Variant Assignment] end subgraph Humanized Multi-Stage Execution Pipeline P --> Q[Stage 1: Read Delay 2–6s] Q --> R[Stage 2: Blue Ticks markMessageAsRead] R --> S[Stage 3: Reaction Delay 1–3s] S --> T[Stage 4: Typing Presence sendPresenceUpdate 'composing' 2–5s] T --> U[Stage 5: Dispatch Reply via Priority Queue] U --> V[Stage 6: Execute Downstream Nodes & Silence Sweeper] end subgraph Observability & UI P --> W[(Record Step Events in DB)] R --> W T --> W U --> W W --> X[Executions Dashboard & Trace Inspector #/executions] W --> Y[Inbox Execution Badges & Drawer] W --> Z[Workflow Editor Run History Panel] end ``` --- ## 2. Inbound Pipeline & Human Anti-Ban Protections ### 1. The Humanized Response Lifecycle When a trigger condition evaluates to **TRUE**: - **Stage 1 (Read Delay: 2–6s)**: Human wait time simulating the recipient noticing the phone notification and opening WhatsApp. - **Stage 2 (Blue Ticks)**: Dispatches `markMessageAsRead`. - **Stage 3 (Reaction Delay: 1–3s)**: Human wait time simulating reading the customer query and preparing a response. - **Stage 4 (Composing Presence: 2–5s)**: Dispatches `sendPresenceUpdate("composing")`. - **Stage 5 (Message Dispatch)**: Dispatches text / media / menu payload. ### 2. Strict Humanization Guardrails - **Unread Retention**: If condition is **FALSE** (no trigger matched), the server **never** marks the conversation as read. The message remains unread for human agents. - **Read-Before-Send Rule**: No automated message is ever sent without first turning blue ticks on. - **Anti-Robotic Separation**: Read receipt and outbound dispatch are **never** fired at the same timestamp. - **Human Takeover Guard**: If a contact is in `bot_status = 'paused_human'`, all automated triggers are suppressed and logged as `execution.suppressed.human_takeover`. - **Direct vs Group Filtering**: - `trigger_personal` only fires on direct 1-on-1 messages. - `trigger_group` only fires on messages where `remoteJid` ends in `@g.us`. - `trigger` / `keyword` matches both (or respects config filter). --- ## 3. Workflow Lifecycle & Management ### 1. Scoping to WhatsApp Number / Session - Every workflow has a `session_id` (`NULL` = All Connected Numbers / Global, or `` = Bound to specific WhatsApp number). - Workflow List and Editor header allow easily assigning or changing the target number. - Inbound trigger evaluation strictly filters workflows active for that session. ### 2. 1-Click Workflow Duplication - **Duplicate button** on Workflow List cards and Editor toolbar. - Deep clones the workflow graph (nodes, configs, positions, and edges). - Names the clone `${Original Name} (Copy)`. - Sets `active: 0` (Draft) for safe offline iteration. ### 3. A/B Variant Testing & Funnel Statistics - Workflows linked to an `Experiment` (`workflows.experiment_id = experiment.id`) act as variants. - Sticky assignment ensures returning contacts always interact with the same variant. - Direct active/draft toggle per variant on the Experiment comparison table. - Shared statistical engine calculates Wilson 95% confidence intervals and Z-test winner recommendations. --- ## 5. Execution Traceability & Live Observability ### 1. Dedicated Executions Dashboard (`#/executions`) - **KPI Summary**: Total Runs, Completed, In-Flight / Waiting Input, Failed, Average Run Duration. - **Filter Bar**: Filter by WhatsApp Session, Workflow, Status, Search (text/phone), Date range. - **Interactive Execution Table**: - Timestamp & Duration (e.g. `2.4s`). - WhatsApp Number & Push Name. - Inbound Message snippet. - Matched Workflow & Variant pill. - Status pill (`Completed`, `Waiting Input`, `Paused Human`, `Failed`). ### 2. Slide-over Execution Trace Drawer - Opens upon clicking any execution row or `⚡ Exec #ID` badge in Inbox. - **Visual Step Timeline**: - `00.0s` 📥 Inbound Message Received. - `00.2s` 🔍 Trigger Matched (Algorithm: Exact, Score: 1.0). - `02.8s` 👁️ Read Receipt: Blue ticks sent (Read Delay: 2.6s). - `04.3s` ⌨️ Presence: Composing simulated (Duration: 3.0s). - `07.3s` 💬 Send Text: Outbound reply dispatched. - `07.3s` 🏁 Completed. - **Variable Inspector**: Live JSON tree of all resolved `vars` and contact attributes. - **Error Inspector**: Exact stack trace / provider error code if failed. --- ## 6. -- A variant IS a workflow (PRD 29): workflows.experiment_id links them.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workflows (
  id            INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  name          TEXT NOT NULL,
  description   TEXT,
  active        INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  session_id    INTEGER REFERENCES sessions(id) ON DELETE SET NULL,
  experiment_id INTEGER REFERENCES experiments(id),
  ai_enabled    INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  created_at    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now')),
  updated_at    TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now'))
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_workflows_session ON workflows (session_id, active);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workflow_nodes (
  id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  workflow_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES workflows(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  node_key    TEXT NOT NULL,
  type        TEXT NOT NULL,
  config      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  position_x  REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  position_y  REAL NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  UNIQUE (workflow_id, node_key)
);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workflow_edges (
  id          INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  workflow_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES workflows(id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
  source_key  TEXT NOT NULL,
  target_key  TEXT NOT NULL,
  handle      TEXT,
  UNIQUE (workflow_id, source_key, target_key, handle)
);

-- Sticky assignment: a contact always lands in the same variant.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS experiment_assignments (
  experiment_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES experiments(id),
  contact_id    INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES contacts(id),
  workflow_id   INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES workflows(id),
  assigned_at   TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now')),
  PRIMARY KEY (experiment_id, contact_id)
);

-- One table for incoming + outgoing. Outgoing-only attribution columns are
-- nullable; this is what makes reply attribution possible (PRD 28).
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS messages (
  id                    INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  session_id            INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES sessions(id),
  contact_id            INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES contacts(id),
  direction             TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (direction IN ('in', 'out')),
  message_type          TEXT NOT NULL,
  text                  TEXT,
  media_id              INTEGER REFERENCES media_assets(id),
  provider_message_id   TEXT UNIQUE,
  in_reply_to_id        INTEGER REFERENCES messages(id),
  workflow_execution_id INTEGER REFERENCES workflow_executions(id),
  node_key              TEXT,
  status                TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'received'
                        CHECK (status IN ('received', 'queued', 'sent', 'delivered', 'read', 'failed')),
  timestamp             TEXT NOT NULL,
  raw_event             TEXT,
  created_at            TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now'))
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_messages_conversation ON messages (session_id, contact_id, timestamp);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_messages_execution    ON messages (workflow_execution_id);

CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS workflow_executions (
  id                 INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  workflow_id        INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES workflows(id),
  session_id         INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES sessions(id),
  contact_id         INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES contacts(id),
  trigger_message_id INTEGER REFERENCES messages(id),
  status             TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'running'
                     CHECK (status IN ('running', 'waiting', 'waiting_input', 'paused_human', 'completed', 'failed', 'cancelled')),
  current_node_key   TEXT,
  vars               TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  reprompt_count     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  silence_followup_at      TEXT,
  silence_sweep_executed   INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  reply_window_expires_at  TEXT,
  started_at         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now')),
  finished_at        TEXT
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_executions_status ON workflow_executions (status, started_at);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_executions_silence ON workflow_executions (status, silence_followup_at, silence_sweep_executed);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_workflow_executions_lookup ON workflow_executions (session_id, contact_id, status);

-- Unified queue: outbound sends, mark-as-read, presence typing, and delay resumes.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS jobs (
  id           INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  type         TEXT NOT NULL CHECK (type IN ('send_message', 'mark_read', 'send_presence', 'resume')),
  execution_id INTEGER NOT NULL REFERENCES workflow_executions(id),
  node_key     TEXT,
  payload      TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  priority     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 1, -- 1: 1-on-1 chats (preemptive), 2: bulk broadcasts
  run_at       TEXT NOT NULL,
  status       TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT 'pending' CHECK (status IN ('pending', 'done', 'failed')),
  attempts     INTEGER NOT NULL DEFAULT 0,
  last_error   TEXT,
  created_at   TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now'))
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_jobs_poll ON jobs (status, priority, run_at);

-- Single audit-trail table covering all event types.
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS events (
  id           INTEGER PRIMARY KEY,
  event_type   TEXT NOT NULL,
  session_id   INTEGER,
  contact_id   INTEGER,
  execution_id INTEGER,
  message_id   INTEGER,
  data         TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT '{}',
  created_at   TEXT NOT NULL DEFAULT (strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now'))
);

CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_events_execution ON events (execution_id, created_at);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_events_execution_ordered ON events (execution_id, id ASC);
CREATE INDEX IF NOT EXISTS idx_events_type      ON events (event_type, created_at);

# ✨ WhatsApp Automation Pipeline, Session Routing & Execution Inspector Complete

### 🚀 Summary of Completed Implementation

We have fully designed, implemented, and verified the complete **WhatsApp Trigger-Based Automation Pipeline**, **WhatsApp Number/Session Scoping**, **Humanized Anti-Ban Sequence**, and **Live Execution Trace Inspector** across backend, shared, and frontend packages.

---

### 1. 🛡️ Humanized Anti-Ban Execution Pipeline
- **Strict Invariant Guard**:
  - If a message condition is **FALSE** (unmatched trigger keywords / inactive flow):
    - The message is **never marked read** (no blue ticks).
    - It remains unread in the physical device & inbox for human attention.
  - If a message condition is **TRUE**:
    - **Step 1 (Human Read Delay)**: Enqueues `mark_read` job with a 2–5s human delay.
    - **Step 2 (Blue Ticks)**: Dispatches Wasender `markMessageAsRead` to turn ticks blue.
    - **Step 3 (Reaction Delay)**: Waits 1–2.5s before composing.
    - **Step 4 (Typing Indicator)**: Calls Wasender `sendPresenceUpdate("composing")` for 2–4s.
    - **Step 5 (Outbound Reply)**: Transports interpolated text/media to the recipient.
  - **Never** sends a reply without turning read on.
  - **Never** marks read and sends a reply at the exact same millisecond.

---

### 2. 📱 WhatsApp Number / Session Scoping
- Added `session_id` to `workflows` database schema and Supabase migrations:
  - [`packages/server/src/db/schema.sql`](file:///home/stevenjossu/wastat/packages/server/src/db/schema.sql)
  - [`supabase/migrations/20260824000001_add_workflow_session_id.sql`](file:///home/stevenjossu/wastat/supabase/migrations/20260824000001_add_workflow_session_id.sql)

- Full UI integration:
  - **Create Modal**: Session selection dropdown in [`WorkflowList.tsx`](file:///home/stevenjossu/wastat/packages/web/src/WorkflowList.tsx).
  - **Workflow Cards**: WhatsApp session badge rendered on each automation.
  - **Workflow Editor**: Number selection dropdown in the header toolbar of [`WorkflowEditor.tsx`](file:///home/stevenjossu/wastat/packages/web/src/WorkflowEditor.tsx).

---

### 3. 🔍 Live Execution Trace Inspector
- **New Web View**: [`packages/web/src/Executions.tsx`](file:///home/stevenjossu/wastat/packages/web/src/Executions.tsx) (`#/executions` tab).
  - **Summary KPI Bar**: Real-time counters for *Total*, *Running*, *Waiting Input (2h)*, *Completed*, *Paused Human*, and *Failed*.
  - **Filter Toolbar**: Instant search across phone numbers, contact names, trigger texts, WhatsApp sessions, and workflow names with 5s live polling.
  - **Interactive Table**: Displays execution ID, contact info, trigger snippet, step count, status, and duration.
  - **Slide-Over Trace Drawer**:
    - Complete chronological timeline of events (`trigger.matched`, `read_receipt.sent`, `presence.sent`, `node.entered`, `condition.evaluated`, `message.sent`, `milestone.reached`, `execution.completed`).

# 🔑 How Authentication Works Under the Hood

### 1. **Per-Message Dispatches (`send-message`, `typing presence`, `mark-as-read`)**:
👉 **Uses the Session API Key (Token) first**, with an automatic fallback to `WASENDER_PAT`:
- When a WhatsApp session (e.g. `105947`) is created or synced, Wasender issues an individual **Session API Key** (`api_key`).
- WaStat stores this session key securely in the database (`sessions.api_key_encrypted`).
- For every outbound message, typing indicator, or blue tick receipt:
  ```http
  POST https://www.wasenderapi.com/api/send-message
  Authorization: Bearer <SESSION_API_KEY>
  ```
- **Failsafe**: If for any reason the session key is missing, WaStat automatically falls back to your global **`WASENDER_PAT`**, ensuring zero dropped messages.

---

### 2. **Account-Level Admin Actions**:
👉 **Uses the `WASENDER_PAT` (Personal Access Token)**:
- **Auto-syncing sessions on boot**: `GET /api/whatsapp-sessions`
- **Auto-configuring Webhooks**: `PUT /api/whatsapp-sessions/:id` (with full events enabled)
- **Generating QR codes & connecting WhatsApp devices**: `POST /api/whatsapp-sessions/:id/connect`
- **Session restarts & disconnects**: `POST /api/whatsapp-sessions/:id/restart`

---

### 💡 Summary:
- **PAT (`WASENDER_PAT`)** manages the account, webhook auto-configuration, and acts as a global safety fallback.
- **Session API Token** isolates sending & receiving per connected WhatsApp number.

# 🛠️ Database Persistence & Step-Level Failure Diagnostics

---

### 1. 💾 Why Your Workflows Reset & How to Make Database 100% Persistent

In Docker / Coolify deployments, when a new commit deploys, Docker creates a fresh container. Unless Coolify is told to retain the storage directory `/app/data`, Docker replaces it with a blank one on each deployment.

#### ✅ Fix in Coolify (Takes 15 Seconds):
1. Open your Coolify Dashboard and go to the **`wastat`** application.
2. Go to **Configuration** → **Storages** (or **Persistent Directories / Volumes**).
3. Click **Add Storage**:
   - **Destination Path (Inside Container)**: `/app/data`
   - **Volume Name**: `wastat-data`
4. Click **Save** and **Deploy**.

> Once this volume is mounted, your workflows, media, sessions, and contacts will **permanently persist across every future deployment or restart!**

---

### 2. 🔍 Step-by-Step Failure Debugging & 1-Click Retry

We have implemented deep diagnostics and failure logging into the engine and trace viewer:

1. **🚨 Step-Level Failure Interception**:
   - If any individual node (Wasender dispatch, media upload, condition, or spintax) throws an error, the engine catches it and records a `job.failed` or `execution.failed` event with:
     - **Failing Node ID / Type**
     - **Exact Error Message** (e.g. invalid phone number, Wasender rate limit, 4xx/5xx response)
     - **Full Stack Trace**
     - **Input payload at the moment of failure**

2. **🔴 Failure Diagnostic Banner in Execution Inspector (`#/executions`)**:
   - When viewing an execution trace, if a step failed, a prominent red card is displayed at the top:
     - Shows the exact node name where execution stopped.
     - Displays the error details without requiring you to inspect server terminal logs.
     - Has an expandable **"View Stack Trace"** accordion.

3. **🔄 1-Click "Retry Step" Button**:
   - You don't have to resend messages or recreate workflows!
   - Just click **`🔄 Retry Step`** directly in the Execution drawer. WaStat will resume execution from that exact step.

---

### 🚀 Both changes are verified and deployed to `origin/main` (`commit 6be6062`).

# 🧪 Implementation Plan: Edge Case Test Lab, Dual-Instance Live Emulation & Humanized Anti-Ban Timing

## Goal Description
Build a full **Edge Case Automation Test Lab & Dual-Instance E2E Emulation Suite** in WaStat V2 to validate every single automation scenario across real connected WhatsApp sessions without manual phone typing:
1. **Full Media Edge Cases**: Video upload & dispatch, image preview & captioning, audio / voice notes, and PDF/document attachments.
2. **Dual-Instance Real-Device Emulation Runner**: Connects 2 live WhatsApp sessions (Session A = Tester Client, Session B = Automation Host), runs automated multi-step conversations between them, and streams execution events live to the dashboard.
3. **Anti-Ban Humanized Timing Engine**: Enforces non-robotic realistic timings:
   - Configurable randomized Read Delay (2s–5s) before sending Blue Ticks (`mark_read`).
   - Configurable randomized Composing/Recording Presence (3s–7s) before dispatching text/voice.
   - Guard against simultaneous or instantaneous bot dispatches.
4. **Interactive In-App Test Lab UI (`#/test-lab`)**: 1-click test launcher for standard test scenarios (Text, Spintax, Image, Video, Audio, Menu, Condition, 2h-Silence, Human Takeover), with real-time pass/fail badges, logs, and deep-link to execution traces.

---

## User Review Required
> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Dual-Instance Testing Requirement**: When running a real-device test in the Test Lab, the app will use Session A to send a WhatsApp message to Session B's physical phone number via Wasender API, triggering Session B's workflow. If only 1 session is connected, the lab also supports **Virtual In-Memory Emulation** so testing works in all environments.

> [!TIP]
> **Anti-Ban Human Timing**: We are adding default random jitter (2,000ms–5,000ms for read delay + 3,000ms–6,000ms for typing presence) to all live automated replies so WhatsApp's heuristic scanners see natural human behavior.

---

## Architecture & Data Flow

```mermaid
sequenceDiagram
    autonumber
    actor User as Sales/Dev Operator
    participant LabUI as Test Lab UI (#/test-lab)
    participant Server as WaStat Server & Test Runner
    participant SessionA as Session A (Client Tester)
    participant Wasender as Wasender API
    participant SessionB as Session B (Bot / Workflow)
    participant Engine as Workflow Engine & Scheduler
    participant Trace as Execution Inspector (#/executions)

    User->>LabUI: Click "Run Edge Case Suite" (e.g. Media + Menu)
    LabUI->>Server: POST /api/test-lab/run-suite { senderSessionId, receiverSessionId, scenarioId }
    Server->>SessionA: Dispatch trigger message with test keyword to Session B's phone
    SessionA->>Wasender: POST /api/send-message (to Session B)
    Wasender-->>SessionB: Webhook message.received
    SessionB->>Engine: Inbound trigger matched!
    
    rect rgb(20, 30, 40)
    Note over Engine: Anti-Ban Humanized Timing
    Engine->>Engine: Wait Random Read Delay (2.5s)
    Engine->>SessionB: Send Blue Ticks (mark_read)
    Engine->>Engine: Wait Random Composing Delay (4.2s)
    Engine->>SessionB: Send Presence ("composing" or "recording")
    end

    Engine->>Wasender: POST /api/send-message (Text / Image / Video / Audio)
    Wasender-->>SessionA: Inbound reply delivered & received
    Engine->>Trace: Log step.entered, read.sent, presence.sent, message.sent
    Server-->>LabUI: SSE / Real-time Test Result (PASS ✓ with timing metrics & media URLs)
```

---

## Proposed Changes

### 1. Backend Engine & Scheduler (`packages/server/`)

#### [MODIFY] `packages/server/src/wasender.ts`
- Enhance `makeWasenderTransport` to support explicit audio voice note flags (`audioUrl` with PTT/voice note metadata), video streaming URLs, document file names, and image captions.
- Add randomized timing helpers: `getRandomDelay(minMs, maxMs)`.

#### [MODIFY] `packages/server/src/engine.ts`
- Add humanized randomized delay queue for all outbound replies:
  - Phase 1: `read_jitter` (random 2s–5s delay before `mark_read`).
  - Phase 2: `presence_jitter` (random 3s–7s delay with `composing` / `recording` status).
  - Phase 3: Outbound message dispatch.
- Ensure audio messages trigger `"recording"` presence instead of `"composing"`.

#### [NEW] `packages/server/src/test-lab.ts`
Create the edge case scenario catalog and runner:
- **Scenario 1: `text_spintax_vars`** — Tests variable interpolation (`{{contact.phone}}`, `{{session.name}}`) and nested spintax variations `{A|{B|C}}`.
- **Scenario 2: `image_media_caption`** — Uploads and dispatches sample PNG/JPEG, verifies public URL resolution, caption delivery, and thumbnail display.
- **Scenario 3: `video_media_streaming`** — Uploads and dispatches sample MP4 video, checks video streaming URL and delivery status.
- **Scenario 4: `audio_voice_note`** — Dispatches audio file with voice note presence ("recording"), checks audio playback.
- **Scenario 5: `document_pdf_attachment`** — Dispatches sample PDF with custom filename and mime-type verification.
- **Scenario 6: `interactive_menu_branching`** — Sends numbered interactive menu, simulates reply option "1", verifies sub-branch execution.
- **Scenario 7: `condition_logic_split`** — Evaluates regex/keyword condition, verifies true/false branching.
- **Scenario 8: `silence_sweeper_2h`** — Fast-forwards clock by 2 hours, triggers `engine.runSilenceSweep()`, asserts `on_silence_2h` branch activation.
- **Scenario 9: `human_takeover_24h`** — Simulates operator manual message, asserts bot status flips to `paused_human`, verifies automation suppression for 24h.
- **Scenario 10: `dual_instance_live_e2e`** — Dispatches live WhatsApp payload from Session A to Session B over real Wasender network, polls for execution completion, and validates end-to-end receipt.

#### [MODIFY] `packages/server/src/api.ts`
- Register Test Lab endpoints:
  - `GET /api/test-lab/scenarios` — Lists all edge case scenarios with descriptions and required assets.
  - `POST /api/test-lab/run` — Runs a specific scenario (dual-instance live or virtual).
  - `POST /api/test-lab/run-all` — Runs the full test suite with consolidated report.
  - `GET /api/test-lab/runs/:id` — Fetches real-time status, step events, and execution trace link.

---

### 2. Frontend Test Lab UI (`packages/web/`)

#### [NEW] `packages/web/src/TestLab.tsx`
Build a high-productivity Test Lab & Scenario Runner:

# 🧪 Implementation Plan: 2-Phase Edge Case Test Lab & Dual-Instance E2E Suite

## Goal Description
Build an in-depth **Edge Case Test Lab & Automation Validator** for WaStat V2 following a strict **Safety-First 2-Phase Execution**:
1. **Phase 1: Virtual In-Memory Emulation & Auto-Fixes (Zero Risk, No Real Numbers)**:
   - Run the complete edge-case matrix (Video, Image, Audio Voice Note, PDF Document, Spintax, Interactive Menu, Conditions, 2h Silence Sweeper, Human Takeover, and Anti-Ban Timing) locally and virtually without touching real WhatsApp numbers.
   - Surface, diagnose, and fix all underlying engine, media handling, and scheduling bugs first.
2. **Phase 2: Real Dual-Instance Device-to-Device Runner**:
   - Once all virtual edge cases pass with 100% reliability, enable the Live Dual-Instance Runner in the app (`#/test-lab`) to orchestrate live WhatsApp messages between Session A and Session B.

---

## Architecture & Phased Workflow

```mermaid
graph TD
    subgraph Phase 1: Virtual Emulation & Fixes
        V1[Scenario 1: Image & Caption] --> VPass[Auto-Fix Engine & Media Pipeline]
        V2[Scenario 2: MP4 Video Streaming] --> VPass
        V3[Scenario 3: Audio Voice Note] --> VPass
        V4[Scenario 4: PDF Document] --> VPass
        V5[Scenario 5: Interactive Menu & Sub-branches] --> VPass
        V6[Scenario 6: 2h Silence Followup] --> VPass
        V7[Scenario 7: Human Takeover 24h Guard] --> VPass
        V8[Scenario 8: Anti-Ban Timing Jitter] --> VPass
        VPass --> Gate{All 10 Virtual Tests 100% Green?}
    end

    subgraph Phase 2: Live Dual-Instance Testing
        Gate -->|Yes| LiveUI[Launch In-App Test Lab UI #/test-lab]
        LiveUI --> RealTest[Session A -> Real WhatsApp -> Session B]
        RealTest --> LiveTrace[View Live Execution Trace #/executions]
    end
```

---

## Detailed Execution Plan

### Phase 1: Virtual Edge Cases & Bug Fixes (Offline / In-Memory)

#### 1. Media Pipeline Edge Cases
- **Image Dispatch**: Uploads sample JPEG/PNG to storage (R2/local fallback), formats `{ to, imageUrl, text }`, verifies public URL and preview thumbnail.
- **MP4 Video Streaming**: Uploads sample MP4, formats `{ to, videoUrl, text }`, checks video mime-type and streaming header.
- **Audio / Voice Note**: Uploads sample MP3/OGG, formats `{ to, audioUrl }`, sets presence to `"recording"` (mimicking human voice recording).
- **Document / PDF Attachment**: Uploads PDF, formats `{ to, documentUrl, fileName }`, tests custom file naming.

#### 2. Anti-Ban Timing & Non-Robotic Delays
- **Read Delay Jitter**: Inbound message -> wait randomized 2,000ms–5,000ms -> send `mark_read` (Blue Ticks).
- **Presence Composing Jitter**: Wait randomized 3,000ms–7,000ms with `"composing"` or `"recording"` presence -> dispatch outbound message.
- **Anti-Simultaneous Guard**: Prevent zero-delay bot replies.

#### 3. Flow Logic Edge Cases
- **Nested Spintax & Vars**: Interpolate `{{contact.name}}`, `{{session.name}}`, `{Hello|Hi|Hey}` with 100% syntactic correctness.
- **Interactive Menu Branching**: Option 1 vs 2 branching, reprompt on invalid choice.
- **Condition Matching**: Exact, regex, fuzzy, and attribute-based conditions.
- **2-Hour Silence Sweeper**: Fast-forward time by 2 hours, assert `on_silence_2h` branch activation.
- **Human Takeover Suppression**: Operator manual message triggers 24h pause on all workflows for that contact.

#### 4. Automated Virtual Test Suite (`packages/server/src/test-lab.test.ts`)
- Implements comprehensive unit & integration tests covering all 10 virtual scenarios with mock transports.

---

### Phase 2: Dual-Instance Real-Device Testing Lab

#### 1. Test Lab API Endpoints (`packages/server/src/test-lab.ts` & `api.ts`)
- `GET /api/test-lab/scenarios` — Catalog of all virtual and live test scenarios.
- `POST /api/test-lab/run` — Executes a scenario (either Virtual Mode or Live Dual-Instance Mode).
- `POST /api/test-lab/run-all` — Runs the full test suite with consolidated results.

#### 2. Frontend Test Lab Dashboard (`packages/web/src/TestLab.tsx`)
- **Mode Toggle**: `[ 🧪 Virtual Simulator Mode ]` vs `[ 📲 Real Number Dual-Instance Mode ]`.
- **Session Pair Selector**: Select Sender (Tester) and Receiver (Bot).
- **Scenario Cards & One-Click Runner**:
  - Run Individual Scenario (e.g. Video, Voice Note, Menu, Timing).
  - Run Full Edge-Case Matrix.
- **Live Output Drawer**:
  - Live progress stepper (⏳ Running -> 🟢 Passed / 🔴 Failed).
  - Timing breakdown (Read Jitter, Typing Delay, Delivery Latency).
  - Media previews (playable video, audio, image thumbnail).
  - Deep-link button: `⚡ View Execution Trace #123`.

---

## Verification Plan

### Automated Tests
```bash
npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build
```
- All 10 virtual edge cases tested in `packages/server/src/test-lab.test.ts`.
- Zero regressions in existing 82 unit/integration tests.

### Manual Verification
1. Open `https://wassflow.orizongroup.online/#/test-lab`.
2. First, run the **Virtual Suite** (verifying all 10 scenarios pass without touching real numbers).
3. Then, switch to **Real Number Mode**, select Session A & Session B, and run live test to observe real WhatsApp message delivery and trace timeline.

# Implementation Plan: Workflow Persistence & Storage Architecture

## Problem Diagnosis: Why Were Workflows Not Persistent?

When you create or edit a workflow in WaStat, there are **two critical persistence boundaries**:

```
[ Browser UI (React Flow) ]  ---(HTTP PUT /api/workflows/:id)--->  [ SQLite DB (/app/data/wastat.db) ]
           │                                                                     │
   Unsaved Drafts in RAM                                            Docker Container Filesystem
   (Lost on tab close / reload)                                     (Lost on Coolify redeployment if 
                                                                     /app/data is not mounted to a Volume)
```

### Root Cause 1: Ephemeral Container File System in Coolify (Primary Cause)
1. In production, WaStat stores all data (workflows, nodes, edges, sessions, contacts, messages, and execution traces) inside a SQLite database at `/app/data/wastat.db`.
2. Every time a `git push` is made to `main`, GitHub Actions triggers a Coolify production deployment.
3. In Docker, when Coolify builds and runs the new container image, **it destroys the old container**.
4. If `/app/data` is **not bound to a Persistent Named Volume** in Coolify, Docker creates an ephemeral container filesystem. When the old container is deleted, the SQLite database file inside it is destroyed, resulting in a clean empty database on the new container!

### Root Cause 2: In-Memory Frontend State (Unsaved Drafts)
1. In `WorkflowEditor.tsx`, canvas edits (dragging nodes, editing text, adding handles) were kept in React component memory state (`useState`).
2. If you refreshed the page, clicked the back arrow, or closed the browser before explicitly clicking the "Save" button, in-flight changes were lost.

---

## User Review Required

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Action Required in Coolify Dashboard (1-Minute Fix)**:
> To ensure SQLite database persistence survives every future Coolify build & deployment:
> 1. Open your Coolify Dashboard -> select the `wastat` application.
> 2. Go to **Storages / Persistent Storage**.
> 3. Add a new Persistent Volume mount:
>    - **Volume Name**: `wastat-data`
>    - **Destination Path**: `/app/data`
> 4. Click **Save** and **Redeploy**.
>
> Once configured, `/app/data/wastat.db` is stored directly on the host server disk and will **never be deleted across new deployments or restarts**.

---

## Proposed Technical Enhancements

To make workflow persistence 100% foolproof both on the server and in the browser UI, we propose the following improvements:

### 1. Frontend: Debounced Auto-Save & LocalStorage Draft Shield
- **File**: `packages/web/src/WorkflowEditor.tsx`
- **What it does**:
  - Adds **Debounced Auto-Save** (automatically saves to SQLite backend 1.5 seconds after any node/edge/text change, displaying an unobtrusive *"All changes saved"* badge).
  - Adds **LocalStorage Draft Backup** (`wastat_draft_{workflowId}`): If your network drops or browser crashes before server response, your work is instantly restored upon reopening the editor.
  - Adds `beforeunload` unsaved changes warning if an active save is in-flight.

### 2. Backup & Portability: 1-Click JSON Workflow Export / Import
- **File**: `packages/web/src/WorkflowList.tsx` & `packages/server/src/api.ts`
- **What it does**:
  - Adds a **`📥 Export Workflows (Backup JSON)`** button: Downloads all your workflows, nodes, and configurations into a single portable `.json` file.
  - Adds an **`📤 Import Workflows`** button: Allows you to restore or migrate any saved workflows with 1 click.

### 3. Server: Seed Default Templates on Clean Install
- **File**: `packages/server/src/index.ts`
- **What it does**:
  - If a fresh database is detected on boot with 0 workflows, it automatically inserts ready-to-use production starter workflows (e.g. *Lead Qualification & VIP Routing*, *Product Catalog & Interactive Menu*), so the platform is never blank.

---

## Verification Plan

### Automated Tests
```bash
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
```

### Manual Verification
1. Open Workflow Editor, drag nodes, edit text -> verify that the *"Auto-saving..."* and *"Saved to database"* indicators update automatically.
2. Hard reload the page (`Ctrl+Shift+R` / `Cmd+Shift+R`) -> verify that all nodes, handles, and configurations are preserved.
3. Test 1-click Export JSON and Import JSON workflow backup.

---

Do you approve this plan? Click **Proceed** to implement the Auto-Save, Draft Shield, and 1-Click Export/Import backup features!

# Implementation Plan: Supabase PostgreSQL & Cloudflare R2 Migration

## Goal Description
Migrate WaStat from local ephemeral SQLite to **Supabase PostgreSQL** and **Cloudflare R2**. This ensures that all workflows, sessions, contacts, messages, and execution traces are permanently persisted in Supabase Cloud, surviving all Coolify container redeployments, restarts, and multi-node instances.

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│                      WaStat Architecture (Post-Migration)                │
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
                                   │
              ┌────────────────────┴────────────────────┐
              ▼                                         ▼
   [ Supabase PostgreSQL ]                    [ Cloudflare R2 ]
   - Permanent Cloud Database                 - Zero-Egress Media Storage
   - Workflows, Nodes, Edges                  - Videos, Images, Voice Notes
   - Contacts, Attributes, Tags               - PDF Catalogs & Attachments
   - Messages, Executions, Events             - Global CDN Public URLs
```

---

## User Review Required

> [!IMPORTANT]
> **Environment Variables Contract on Coolify**:
> The following environment variables must be configured in your Coolify Application settings (`wassflow.orizongroup.online`):
> 
> **Supabase PostgreSQL**:
> - `DATABASE_URL` (or `SUPABASE_URL` + `SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY`)
> 
> **Cloudflare R2**:
> - `R2_ACCOUNT_ID`
> - `R2_ACCESS_KEY_ID`
> - `R2_SECRET_ACCESS_KEY`
> - `R2_BUCKET_NAME`
> - `R2_PUBLIC_URL`

> [!TIP]
> **Zero-Breakage Compatibility**:
> In-memory SQLite (`:memory:`) will remain available as an automated fallback for unit tests and local mock development (`npm test`), guaranteeing all unit test suites run in under 5 seconds with 100% pass rate.

---

## Proposed Changes

### 1. Database Abstraction & Supabase PostgreSQL Provider
- **File**: `packages/server/src/db/client.ts` [NEW]
  - Provides a unified Database interface `DbClient` that supports both Supabase PostgreSQL (via `postgres` / Supabase SDK) and SQLite (`better-sqlite3`).
  - Auto-detects `DATABASE_URL` or `SUPABASE_URL` on server boot:
    - If present $\rightarrow$ connects to Supabase PostgreSQL and runs migrations from `supabase-schema.sql`.
    - If absent $\rightarrow$ falls back to SQLite (`wastat.db` or `:memory:`).

### 2. Server Entrypoint (`packages/server/src/index.ts`)
- [MODIFY] Initialize database via `createDatabaseClient()`.
- Run schema migration on startup in Supabase PostgreSQL (`supabase/migrations/20260824000000_wastat_v2_schema.sql`).
- Pass unified DB client to `buildApp`, `createEngine`, and `makeWasenderTransport`.

### 3. Engine & Scheduler (`packages/server/src/engine.ts` & `packages/server/src/scheduler.ts`)
- [MODIFY] Adapt SQL query builders and transactions to work seamlessly across PostgreSQL and SQLite (handling PostgreSQL `TIMESTAMPTZ`, JSONB, and parameterized queries).

### 4. API Routes (`packages/server/src/api.ts`, `sessions.ts`, `routes/broadcasts.ts`, `routes/ai.ts`)
- [MODIFY] Update workflow CRUD, session queries, executions trace logging, and broadcast scheduling to use the unified database adapter.

### 5. Media Suite (`packages/server/src/media.ts`)
- Ensure `createStorageFromEnv()` defaults to Cloudflare R2 with AWS S3 SDK whenever `R2_ACCOUNT_ID` and keys are provided, uploading media and saving public CDN URLs in Supabase `media_assets`.

---

## Verification Plan

### Automated Tests
```bash
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
```

### Live Cloud Verification
1. Server connects to Supabase on boot and outputs `[DB] Connected to Supabase PostgreSQL`.
2. Create a workflow with nodes & edges in the UI $\rightarrow$ Verify record appears in Supabase `workflows`, `workflow_nodes`, `workflow_edges` tables.
3. Upload an image / video / audio $\rightarrow$ Verify file is uploaded to Cloudflare R2 bucket and accessible via `R2_PUBLIC_URL`.
4. Trigger redeploy or restart container $\rightarrow$ Verify created workflows and sessions remain 100% intact from Supabase!

---

Do you approve this plan? Click **Proceed** to start the Supabase & Cloudflare R2 migration!

# Comprehensive Implementation Plan: Supabase PostgreSQL & Cloudflare R2 Migration

## 🎯 Goal Description
Migrate WaStat from local ephemeral SQLite to **Supabase PostgreSQL** and **Cloudflare R2**, permanently eliminating data loss on Coolify redeployments and enabling real-time multi-operator synchronization and zero-egress media streaming.

---

## 🔎 Deep Audit of Overlooked Edge Cases & Technical Differences

During our deep codebase inspection, we identified the following critical differences between SQLite and Supabase PostgreSQL that must be addressed:

### 1. Boolean & Integer Type Mismatches
- **SQLite**: Booleans are stored as integers (`active = 1` or `0`, `silence_sweep_executed = 0`).
- **PostgreSQL**: Strict `BOOLEAN` type (`active = true` or `false`). Inserting `1` into a PostgreSQL boolean column throws a syntax error.
- **Fix**: Normalize all boolean reads and writes in query helpers (`Boolean(val)`).

### 2. JSON & JSONB Handling
- **SQLite**: JSON columns (`vars`, `config`, `payload`, `data`) are stored as raw `TEXT`.
- **PostgreSQL**: Columns are typed as `JSONB`. PostgreSQL driver (`postgres`) automatically serializes/deserializes JSON objects without manual `JSON.parse`/`JSON.stringify` duplication.
- **Fix**: Handle both stringified and native JSON objects seamlessly in repository layers.

### 3. Timestamps & Timezones
- **SQLite**: `strftime('%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%fZ', 'now')` UTC string.
- **PostgreSQL**: `TIMESTAMPTZ` with `now()`.
- **Fix**: Use ISO-8601 UTC strings across all date comparisons so both engines format timestamps identically.

### 4. Primary Key Auto-Increment & Insertion Returns
- **SQLite**: `INTEGER PRIMARY KEY` $\rightarrow$ `info.lastInsertRowid`.
- **PostgreSQL**: `BIGSERIAL PRIMARY KEY` $\rightarrow$ `RETURNING id`.
- **Fix**: Unified insert helper that returns `{ id: number }` across both engines.

### 5. Binary Keys (`BYTEA` vs `BLOB`)
- **SQLite**: `api_key_encrypted BLOB`.
- **PostgreSQL**: `api_key_encrypted BYTEA`.
- **Fix**: Use `Buffer` conversion helpers when reading/writing session encryption keys.

### 6. Cloudflare R2 Storage & Public CDN Normalization
- **Issue**: Missing `https://` prefix or trailing slash in `R2_PUBLIC_URL` causes broken image/video links in WhatsApp.
- **Fix**: Normalize `R2_PUBLIC_URL` (strip trailing slash, ensure protocol) in `media.ts`.

### 7. Supabase Realtime Subscription in Inbox
- **Issue**: Frontend previously relied solely on HTTP polling.
- **Fix**: Enable Supabase Realtime listener in `packages/web` if `VITE_SUPABASE_URL` and `VITE_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` are provided, with seamless polling fallback.

---

## 🏗️ Architecture & Component Plan

```
                                  ┌────────────────────────┐
                                  │      Fastify Server    │
                                  └───────────┬────────────┘
                                              │
                    ┌─────────────────────────┴─────────────────────────┐
                    ▼                                                   ▼
       ┌────────────────────────┐                          ┌────────────────────────┐
       │   Database Layer       │                          │   Media Storage Layer  │
       │   (DbClient Adapter)   │                          │   (StorageProvider)    │
       └────────────┬───────────┘                          └────────────┬───────────┘
                    │                                                   │
        ┌───────────┴───────────┐                           ┌───────────┴───────────┐
        ▼                       ▼                           ▼                       ▼
 [ Supabase PostgreSQL ]   [ SQLite :memory: ]        [ Cloudflare R2 ]      [ Local Disk ]
 (Production Cloud)       (Unit Tests / Fast CI)      (Production CDN)       (Offline Fallback)
```

---

## 📝 Proposed File Changes

### 1. Database Layer (`packages/server/src/db/`)
- **`packages/server/src/db/client.ts` [NEW]**:
  - Unified `DbClient` interface abstracting queries, inserts, transactions, and parameter bindings.
  - Automatically initializes **Supabase PostgreSQL** when `DATABASE_URL` or `SUPABASE_URL` is set.
  - Automatically initializes **SQLite** for unit tests or when no cloud credentials exist.
  - Runs startup migrations from `supabase-schema.sql` on boot.
- **`packages/server/src/db/supabase-schema.sql` [MODIFY]**:
  - Ensure all 19 production tables, foreign keys, and indexes are up to date.

### 2. Core Server & Engine (`packages/server/src/`)
- **`packages/server/src/index.ts` [MODIFY]**:
  - Initialize `db` via `createDatabaseClient()`.
  - Log active database provider (`Supabase PostgreSQL` vs `SQLite`).
- **`packages/server/src/engine.ts` [MODIFY]**:
  - Adapt queries for boolean, JSONB, and `RETURNING id` compatibility.
- **`packages/server/src/scheduler.ts` [MODIFY]**:
  - Ensure priority job queue queries run smoothly across PostgreSQL and SQLite.
- **`packages/server/src/media.ts` [MODIFY]**:
  - Enforce Cloudflare R2 URL normalization and S3 bucket connection validation.

### 3. API & Webhooks (`packages/server/src/`)
- **`packages/server/src/api.ts` [MODIFY]**:
  - Update workflow CRUD, executions trace logging, and experiment queries to use `DbClient`.
- **`packages/server/src/webhook.ts` [MODIFY]**:
  - Ensure idempotency deduplication works across both databases.

---

## 🧪 Verification Plan

### Automated Tests
```bash
npm run typecheck
npm test
npm run build
```

### Live Verification
1. Server connects to Supabase on boot and outputs `[DB] Connected to Supabase PostgreSQL`.
2. Create, edit, and duplicate a workflow $\rightarrow$ Verify records in Supabase Dashboard.
3. Upload media (image, audio, video, PDF) $\rightarrow$ Verify upload in Cloudflare R2 bucket.
4. Restart/redeploy container $\rightarrow$ Verify all workflows and sessions remain intact.

---

Please review and approve this updated plan to begin the migration!

   - SQLite uses `1` / `0`, whereas PostgreSQL requires strict `true` / `false`. Inserting integers into boolean columns (`active`, `ai_enabled`, `silence_sweep_executed`) would throw a type error in PostgreSQL. Query builders will normalize boolean values.
2. **JSONB vs TEXT Columns**:
   - PostgreSQL uses native `JSONB` for `vars`, `config`, and `data` columns.
3. **Primary Key Auto-Increment & Returns**:
   - SQLite uses `lastInsertRowid`, while PostgreSQL uses `RETURNING id`.
4. **Binary Session Keys**:
   - SQLite `BLOB` vs PostgreSQL `BYTEA` conversion for `api_key_encrypted`.
5. **Cloudflare R2 URL Normalization**:
   - Auto-formatting and protocol checks (`https://`) on `R2_PUBLIC_URL` to prevent broken media URLs.
6. **Automatic Boot Migrations**:
   - Auto-executing table setup on Supabase on startup if tables are not yet created.

---

# Master Architecture & Performance Plan: WaStat V2

## 🚀 Architectural Vision & High-Performance Targets
Transform WaStat into an enterprise-grade WhatsApp Automation & Sales Intelligence Engine capable of processing **10,000+ messages/day** across multiple phone numbers with **zero data loss, sub-50ms webhook acknowledgment, resilient anti-ban safety, and instant UI rendering**.

---

## 🏛️ System Architecture Overview

```
                          ┌─────────────────────────────┐
                          │   Wasender Webhook Inbound  │
                          └──────────────┬──────────────┘
                                         │ (Sub-50ms ACK)
                                         ▼
                          ┌─────────────────────────────┐
                          │  Fastify Fast Webhook Ingest│
                          └──────────────┬──────────────┘
                                         │
                 ┌───────────────────────┼───────────────────────┐
                 ▼                       ▼                       ▼
      ┌────────────────────┐  ┌────────────────────┐  ┌────────────────────┐
      │  Supabase Postgres │  │  Priority Job Queue│  │  Cloudflare R2 CDN │
      │  (PgBouncer Pool)  │  │  (Anti-Ban Timing) │  │  (Zero Egress Media)
      └────────────────────┘  └──────────┬─────────┘  └────────────────────┘
                                         │
                                         ▼
                              ┌────────────────────┐
                              │  Wasender Outbound │
                              │ (Random Jitter 5s) │
                              └────────────────────┘
```

---

## ⚡ 6 Core Performance & Architecture Pillars

### Pillar 1: Supabase Connection Pooling & Index Optimization
1. **Supavisor / PgBouncer Connection Pooling**:
   - Use Supabase transaction pooling port (`6543` / `?pgbouncer=true`) with `postgres` client pool limits (`max: 10`, `idle_timeout: 20s`) to prevent connection exhaustion during traffic spikes.
2. **High-Performance Compound Indexes**:
   - `CREATE INDEX idx_executions_silence_sweep ON workflow_executions (status, silence_followup_at, silence_sweep_executed)` $\rightarrow$ eliminates full table scans during the 2-hour silence sweeper loop.
   - `CREATE INDEX idx_events_execution_timeline ON events (execution_id, created_at ASC)` $\rightarrow$ instant retrieval of full execution trace drawer.
   - `CREATE INDEX idx_messages_idempotency ON messages (provider_message_id)` $\rightarrow$ $O(1)$ duplicate webhook rejection.
3. **N+1 Query Elimination**:
   - Use PostgreSQL `json_agg` and subquery joins to fetch workflows with all nodes and edges in **1 single query** instead of 3 sequential roundtrips.

---

### Pillar 2: Asynchronous Sub-50ms Webhook Pipeline
1. **Zero-Block Ingestion**:
   - Webhook endpoint verifies HMAC / session key $\rightarrow$ writes message row $\rightarrow$ replies `200 { ok: true }` in **$<20\text{ms}$**.
   - Workflow execution matching and scheduler triggers execute asynchronously in background micro-tasks so Wasender never experiences timeouts or triggers retry loops.
2. **Strict Idempotency Guard**:
   - Inbound `provider_message_id` deduplication prevents double-triggering when webhooks are re-delivered.

---

### Pillar 3: Anti-Ban Token Bucket & Humanized Jitter
1. **Per-Session Concurrency Limiter**:
   - Enforce $\ge 5\text{s}$ cooldown between consecutive outgoing messages on the same WhatsApp phone number.
2. **Realistic Human Simulation Pipeline**:
   - Inbound Received $\rightarrow$ Random Read Delay (`1.5s – 3.5s`) $\rightarrow$ Send Blue Ticks (`mark_read`) $\rightarrow$ Send Presence Update (`composing` for text/media or `recording` for voice notes, `2.0s – 5.0s`) $\rightarrow$ Dispatch Message.
3. **Priority Preemption**:
   - Inbound 1-on-1 customer replies (Priority 1) immediately pause background bulk broadcast dispatches (Priority 2).

---

### Pillar 4: Cloudflare R2 Media & Streaming CDN
1. **Direct Stream Uploads**:
   - Stream audio, video, and PDF uploads directly to Cloudflare R2 using AWS S3 SDK with `multipartUpload` support, keeping Node.js memory footprint below 50MB.
2. **Edge Cache Headers**:
   - Set `Cache-Control: public, max-age=31536000, immutable` and `Accept-Ranges: bytes` on R2 media objects for lightning-fast media playback in WhatsApp and browsers.
3. **Automatic URL Protocol & Trailing Slash Sanitization**:
   - Normalize `R2_PUBLIC_URL` on boot to guarantee clean CDN URLs.

---

### Pillar 5: Frontend Bundle Splitting & UI Performance
1. **React Lazy Loading & Code-Splitting**:
   - Split `WorkflowEditor`, `TestLab`, `Executions`, `Broadcasts`, and `Inbox` into async chunks using `React.lazy()` and `Suspense`.
   - Shrinks initial bundle size from **518 kB $\rightarrow$ $<120\text{ kB}$**, resulting in **$<300\text{ms}$** First Contentful Paint.
2. **React Flow Node Virtualization**:
   - Set `onlyRenderVisibleElements={true}` and debounce canvas transform updates so workflows with 100+ nodes render at 60 FPS.
3. **Debounced Auto-Save & LocalStorage Resilience**:
   - 1.5s debounce on workflow canvas edits + `localStorage` draft shield to prevent lost work on accidental page reload.

---

### Pillar 6: AI Sales Co-Pilot & Flywheel Resiliency
1. **Groq Llama 3.3 70B Optimization**:
   - Enforce strict 8-second timeout with fallback responses so LLM rate-limits never block customer conversational flow.
2. **Prompt Template Memoization**:
   - Memoize static prompt frames and product catalog tokens to minimize token overhead and latency.

---

## 📋 Implementation Roadmap

| Phase | Milestone | Expected Impact |
|---|---|---|
| **Phase 1** | Supabase PostgreSQL Connection Pool & Missing Indexes | Permanent cloud persistence & zero-latency queries |
| **Phase 2** | Cloudflare R2 CDN Normalization & Direct Streaming | Zero egress costs & instant WhatsApp media playback |
| **Phase 3** | Fast Webhook Ingestion & Anti-Ban Token Bucket Queue | Zero timeouts, no duplicate runs, anti-ban safety |
| **Phase 4** | Frontend Code-Splitting & React Flow 60fps Optimization | 4x faster initial page load & smooth canvas editing |

---

## 🧪 Verification & Benchmark Plan

1. **Automated Tests**: `npm run typecheck && npm test && npm run build` (100% pass required).
2. **Load Benchmark**: Simulate 100 concurrent incoming webhooks $\rightarrow$ Assert 100% received with $<50\text{ms}$ latency and zero dropped messages.
3. **Bundle Size Check**: Verify production bundle chunk sizes are split below Vite warning thresholds.

---

Do you approve this Master Architecture & Performance Plan? Click **Proceed** to start implementation!

# Implementation Plan: Realtime WhatsApp Inbox, Rich Chat Preview & Execution Logs

## 🎯 Goal Description
Build a pixel-perfect, high-converting **WhatsApp Realtime Live Inbox** and **Execution Diagnostic Console** powered by **Supabase Realtime PostgreSQL**, featuring rich WhatsApp message bubble previews (images, audio waveforms, video players, PDF attachments, numbered menus, blue ticks), live multi-operator synchronization, AI Co-Pilot suggestions, and deep step-level execution logs with 1-click retries.

---

## 🎨 WhatsApp Chat Preview & Bubble Design

```
┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐
│  👤 Marcus Aurelius (+1 555-019-9832)  [ 🟢 Bot Active | ⏸️ Pause 24h ] │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│                                                                         │
│  [Inbound Lead]                                                         │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐                 │
│  │ Hi! I saw your Instagram ad for luxury villas.     │ 14:02           │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘                 │
│                                                                         │
│                                                     [Automated Bot]     │
│                 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│                 │ ⚡ Phase 1: Video Hook (Variant A)                   │ │
│                 │ ───────────────────────────────────                 │ │
│                 │ 🎥 [▶ Video Player: 45s Ultra-Luxury Villa Demo]    │ │
│                 │                                                     │ │
│                 │ Welcome Marcus! Here is our 2026 collection.        │ │
│                 │ 14:02 ✓✓                                            │ │
│                 └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                         │
│                                                     [Voice Note]        │
│                 ┌─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐ │
│                 │ 🎙️ ▶ ══════●────────────── 0:24                     │ │
│                 │ 14:03 ✓✓ (Blue Ticks)                               │ │
│                 └─────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘ │
│                                                                         │
│  ┌────────────────────────────────────────────────────┐                 │
│  │ Do you have beachfront options with pools?         │ 14:05           │
│  └────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘                 │
│                                                                         │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ ✨ AI Suggestion: "Yes Marcus! All our $1M+ villas include private      │
│    infinity pools. Would you like our beachfront PDF catalog?" [Send ⚡] │
├─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┤
│ [ 📎 Attach Media ] [ Type a message...                             ] [➤]│
└─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────┘
```

---

## 🏗️ Technical Architecture & Pillars

### 1. Supabase Realtime Database Pub/Sub
- **Database Publication**:
  ```sql
  ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE messages;
  ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE contacts;
  ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE workflow_executions;
  ALTER PUBLICATION supabase_realtime ADD TABLE events;
  ```
- **Frontend Realtime Channel (`packages/web/src/Inbox.tsx`)**:
  - Subscribes to `supabase.channel('live-inbox')` on `postgres_changes`.
  - When an inbound webhook writes a message, all open operator inboxes update **instantly in $<100\text{ms}$** without polling.
